perspective:
From Ethan’s perspective, I know/observed/heard:

- I am Ethan Mohamud, a plumber. Gary Guo is my close, long-time friend; we met in middle school and have relied on each other for support. He is a doctor.
- I noticed Gary was working excessively long hours at the hospital, often skipping meals and sacrificing sleep. I invited him to a weekend retreat to relax. Gary said he appreciated my concern but couldn’t go because there was too much to do at the hospital.
- During the retreat, I saw Gary acting restless and avoiding talk about work. I suspected something more than professional obligations was going on. I confronted him, saying he could tell me anything. Gary said it was complicated and he didn’t want to burden me. He then opened up about pressures from managing a new department and personal challenges he was facing.
- I suggested prioritizing his tasks and delegating responsibilities. Gary agreed and said he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself too.
- Over the following months, I regularly checked in with Gary about his progress and remaining challenges. I saw him making efforts to change, felt hopeful and proud, and continued offering support. Gary told me things were better, he was less overwhelmed, and he had time for a movie last weekend.
- After about a year, I saw Gary managing better on his own. I felt satisfied and happy. I told him I was always a call away but knew he had it handled. Gary thanked me, said he couldn’t have done it without my support, and felt more in control now.
